findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 (and the same change in account/messages_lt.properties totpStep1) was replaced with 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see instructions in the wrong language on the TOTP setup screens; the previous Lithuanian text that contained the illegal anchors should have been translated/adapted, not replaced with the Italian string.

findings.title: MessageFormat choice syntax breaks JS i18next interpolation
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from the JS UI convention 'Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).' to Java MessageFormat syntax 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.'. Every other placeholder in this account-ui file (and in js/apps/admin-ui messages_en.properties, changed the same way) uses {{n}} for the React/i18next renderer, which does not evaluate {n,choice,...}; users in the account/admin consoles will see the raw placeholders/choice expression instead of the interpolated counts. The choice/plural form is only valid for the server-side themes properties.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart crashes verifier instead of reporting a verification error
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file purely by string replacement on the absolute path and throws RuntimeException('unable to read file ...') when that derived file does not exist. verify() only catches IOException and converts it to MojoExecutionException, so a locale file whose English source lives elsewhere or whose name does not match the '_xx.properties' -> '_en.properties' pattern (e.g. a messages.properties without locale suffix, or a new theme location) aborts the whole plugin run with an unhandled stack trace instead of producing a collected verification message or a clear Mojo failure.

findings.title: HTML allowance is keyed only to presence of any HTML in English, not the tags actually used
findings.body: containsHtml() returns true if the English value contains any '<[a-z]+...>' tag, and then POLICY_SOME_HTML unconditionally allows br/p/strong/b in the translation even if the English string used none of them (for example an English value containing only an <a> anchor, which is stripped by santizeAnchors). Conversely, legitimate English markup outside br/p/strong/b/a is rejected in translations even when copied verbatim. This makes the check both permissive for injected formatting tags not present in the source and prone to false positives, weakening the stated guarantee that only HTML present in the English source may appear in translations.
